lines.text: The monsoon was rough on the little bridge. Let's not rush it. Walk it first and tell me what looks tired.
Good eyes. The top gave out, the beams bent, and the supports lost their footing.
Let's see what can be reused. Good repair starts by respecting what is already here.
That'll do for a start. Old materials can be honest, if we test them.
Now the quiet part. Add weight slowly and let each piece tell on itself.
Your notebook caught the story. Steel held, composite stayed light, and wood liked a shorter reach.
Simple beam or triangle truss, either can work. Supports first. Always give the weight somewhere to go.
Step lightly... there. Feel that? The weight found its way home.
The neighbors can cross again. Before we celebrate, let's read the bridge like engineers. Repairs belong to people, but the forces still need a safe path.

lines.title: Getting Over the Abyss
lines.text: Mr. Chen opens a worn engineering spread. "A bridge is a promise between two banks. A beam lies across the gap, an arch squeezes force into its supports, suspension and cable-stayed bridges use tension, and combination bridges borrow more than one trick."

slides.title: Why Bridges Exist
slides.body: A bridge is a force path from traveler, to deck, to supports, to ground.
slides.teaching_point: A bridge is not just a deck. It is a load path.

slides.title: Six Bridge Families
slides.body: Beams bend, arches compress, frames lock members, cables pull in tension, and trusses use repeated triangles.
slides.teaching_point: Different shapes handle compression, tension, and bending differently.

slides.title: Main Parts
slides.body: The superstructure carries the deck. Abutments hold the ends. A pier helps carry a long span.
slides.teaching_point: Name the parts before you decide what failed.

slides.title: Rectangles Can Rack
slides.body: A rectangle can lean into a parallelogram when pushed from the side.
slides.teaching_point: Wobble is a shape problem, not just a material problem.

slides.title: Why Triangles
slides.body: A triangle resists changing shape, so truss braces share load instead of letting the bridge fold.
slides.teaching_point: Triangle trusses turn wobble into shared tension and compression.

slides.title: Trace The Load Path
slides.body: Trace the bike load through the deck, into triangle braces, then into supports and steady ground.
slides.teaching_point: The right bridge is the one whose shape and supports match the site.

lines.text: A rectangle likes to lean. A triangle holds its ground because changing its shape means stretching or compressing a side. That is why trusses use repeated triangles.
Now trace it: feet push the deck, the deck pushes the triangle braces, the braces carry force to the supports, and the supports press it into steady ground. That is the bridge doing its quiet work.

other_npc_lines.text: Look for cracks and rust first. A bargain that fails is not a bargain.
Hey, I can cross again. It feels less wobbly than the old one.
That little bridge matters more than it looks. Folks use it every day.
